name: Amphotericin B
mechanism: Binds ergosterol and disrupts fungal cell membranes
dosing: IV formulations vary; lipid formulations reduce nephrotoxicity
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to amphotericin B or formulation components
interactions: Concurrent nephrotoxins (e.g., aminoglycosides, calcineurin inhibitors) increase risk of renal injury; monitor co-administered drugs closely
monitoring: Frequent monitoring of renal function, serum electrolytes (potassium, magnesium), and for infusion-related reactions during and after administration; consider pre-medication for infusion reactions
pregnancy: Use only if benefits outweigh risks; specialist infectious disease/obstetric advice required
sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity (dose-limiting), infusion-related fever and rigors, electrolyte disturbances (hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia); lipid formulations reduce nephrotoxicity
clinicalPearls: Reserved for serious systemic fungal infections; consider lipid formulations to reduce nephrotoxicity and monitor electrolytes closely
indication: Serious systemic fungal infections where alternative agents are unsuitable
